root_cause.text: The function `nfsd_attrs_valid()` only checked for iattr changes and security labels, not POSIX ACLs, so when a file creation included only an ACL attribute, it returned false and prevented `nfsd_setattr()` from applying the ACL.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: *"nfsd_attrs_valid() checks only for iattr changes and security labels, but not POSIX ACLs. When only an ACL is present, the function returns false, nfsd_setattr() is skipped, and the POSIX ACL is never applied to the inode."* The patch diff adds `attrs->na_pacl || attrs->na_dpacl` to the return condition, confirming the missing check.

vuln_statements.explanation: The struct field na_labelerr exists but the pre-fix version lacked fields for POSIX ACL pointers (na_pacl, na_dpacl), making the validation function incomplete.
The struct field na_aclerr exists but the pre-fix version lacked fields for POSIX ACL pointers, so the validation function could not check ACL attributes.
The struct definition ends without including na_pacl and na_dpacl fields in the pre-fix version, causing nfsd_attrs_valid() to not check ACLs.
The free function signature, introduced in the fix to release ACLs; the pre-fix version lacked this and any ACL handling.
This line shows the corrected version freeing na_pacl; the pre-fix version had no such check, allowing ACLs to be ignored.
